context: Naoko teaches Hina-young how to properly tie a yukata.
purpose: Aunt teaching teen traditional dress for summer festival.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: Hina — first time wearing a yukata?
lines.style: Warm, brassy Kansai drawl. Bright fondness in the opening. Teasing lilt at the question, like she already knows the answer and loves that she does.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Breathless with anticipation. Quick, eager attack on the opening syllable. Slight tremor underneath the brightness — genuine excitement mixed with first-time jitters.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 帯、ようけ気つけて結ぶで。
lines.en: The obi — tie it carefully, yeah?
lines.style: Practical and animated. Kansai lilt on the directive. Not stern — a teacher's attention, hands-on, making sure the kid gets it right because it matters.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: はい、おばちゃん、お願い!
lines.style: Small, trusting voice. Soft at the opening. Slight lift at the end — asking, leaning into the request without hesitation. The comfort of being cared for by someone bigger.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 夏祭り、めっちゃ似合うで!
lines.en: Summer festival — you look absolutely beautiful in it!
lines.style: Warm, proud exhale on the opening. Kansai generosity in the delivery. Slow enough to let the compliment land. Not performative — genuine admiration from someone who loves her.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Bright gratitude with a soft undercurrent. Quick smile in the voice. Genuine pleasure, not exuberant — the quiet contentment of being seen and admired by someone she loves.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: Go have the time of your life tonight!
lines.style: Loud, brassy send-off. Open-hearted encouragement. Full-chested delivery — the kind of aunt who means it. Warm volume, not harsh. The blessing of someone rooting for you.
